artifacts.summary: Audit of 16 file_scope files' inline specs/state.json write sites (68 in-scope sites re-measured, vs. task's stated ~56 approximate baseline), confirms state-write.sh mechanism is complete and needs no changes, identifies fold/don't-fold precedent in commands/review.md, session_id availability per file, and the scope boundary that specs/archive/state.json and vault-path writes are excluded from this task's verification bar.

memory_candidates.content: state-write.sh (agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/state-write.sh) hardcodes STATE_FILE to specs/state.json with no --file override. Any future task converting specs/archive/state.json or vault-root state.json writers (e.g. inside skill-todo's vault operation) needs to either extend state-write.sh with a --file argument or accept those writers stay hand-rolled indefinitely -- they are a structurally distinct, separately out-of-scope surface from the specs/state.json conversion work.

The self-generating session_id fallback pattern (sess_$(date +%s)_$(od -An -N3 -tx1 /dev/urandom | tr -d ' ')) is established in five core scripts: manage-topics.sh, archive-task.sh, reconcile-artifacts.sh, orchestrate-predispatch-review.sh, skill-base.sh. Use this exact snippet (guarded by an emptiness check on the session_id variable) when converting a script or command that lacks an inherited session_id, rather than inventing a new format.

commands/review.md is the canonical precedent for the state-write.sh --regen-todo fold-vs-don't-fold judgment call: lines 628-655 show a write deliberately NOT folded (because manage-topics.sh set must run between the write and the regen), and lines 795-826 show a write folded (because nothing but the regen follows). Future state-write.sh conversions should imitate these two examples rather than defaulting to always-fold or always-separate.
